The UN High Commissioner for Refugees visited quake-affected areas on October 3. Miami-Dade’s Hispanic Heritage Month kickoff featured a painting fundraiser for earthquake relief.

news.headline: Takeaways from AP investigation into collapse of housing towers during Venezuela's earthquakes
news.body: The collapse of public housing in Venezuela's La Guaira state after two June earthquakes is linked to decisions made in 2010. Experts say the government rushed to build apartments on unstable soil after mudslides displaced over 100,000 people. The buildings couldn't withstand the earthquakes, which scientists have now determined led to one of the largest ground motions ever documented in the world. The area’s proximity to a fault line and the height of the buildings increased risks. The government hasn't provided crucial data or blueprints and experts urge a careful rebuilding approach. They warn the cost of earthquake-resistant construction may deter future development. Over 6,500 people died in the June event.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

logs.summary:
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region near Ende on August 14, 2026, toppling buildings and killing at least two people. The shallow quake triggered a tsunami warning for four provinces, prompting mass evacuations before the alert was later lifted. Several strong aftershocks were reported.
The death toll from the magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Ende, Indonesia has risen to at least 38, with dozens injured and many buildings collapsed or damaged. Rescuers are searching for survivors in affected areas, and tsunami waves of less than 1 meter were recorded in several locations before the warning was lifted.

news.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia, tsunami warning issued - West Hawaii Today
news.body: JAKARTA (Reuters) — An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and several aftershocks struck off the coast of eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the nation’s geophysics agency BMKG said, while tsunami waves of less than 1 metre (3 feet) were recorded in several areas. Many rushed from their homes, but there were no initial reports of damage from the quake, which was felt strongly for around one minute in regions such as Nagekeo and Bima, said Dodi Yuleova, the spokesperson for the national disaster mitigation agency. A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as located at a port in Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed parts of a building collapsing in dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street. A hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed. BMKG recorded the first quake at 4:58 a.m. (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by several aftershocks.

incidents.summary:
Rasuwagadhi Hydro provided Rs 500,000 per family to employees who went missing or died in the Bhotekoshi flood. The Nepali community in North Alabama donated $50,000 to the Prime Minister's Relief Fund for flood victims, while the New Zealand-Nepal Society contributed Rs 12.6 million for relief and rehabilitation. The government also declared flood-affected local levels in Gorkha, Baglung, and Dhading as disaster crisis areas.
New reports highlight the ongoing psychological and logistical recovery from the Bagmati floods. An article warns that graphic flood videos on social media are increasing mental stress among children, while UNICEF is working to meet the urgent needs of over 32,000 affected children. A feature story details the difficult resettlement prospects facing survivors like Chheku Lama, who lost his home in the disaster.

logs.summary: A glacier collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border triggered devastating flash floods and mudslides on August 26, 2026, sweeping through several communities in the Bagmati region. The disaster has killed hundreds of people (with death tolls reported between 350 and 500) and left over 1,300 missing, including dozens of foreign nationals. Rescue teams are searching for survivors while authorities warn of additional flood risks from a newly formed lake, and international aid is arriving to support relief efforts.

news.headline: Aug. 27: Flash Flooding Overwhelms Nepal, and Jury Deliberates in Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Trial
news.body: Devastating flash floods and mudslides wreaked havoc along the Nepal-China border this week, leaving hundreds dead and more than 1,000 missing. More than 500 foreigners are among the missing, including, by one estimate, roughly 65 Americans. NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer explains why the destruction happened without warning and what role climate change may have played. Then, jury deliberations are underway in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who killed her three young children. While Clancy doesn’t dispute the killings, her defense team is arguing that she shouldn’t be held criminally responsible because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. But the prosecution insists she acted intentionally and deliberately. As the jury weighs a set of complex outcomes, NBC News legal analyst Misty Marris breaks down what evidence and testimony from the five-week trial could be key to reaching a verdict. Finally, 2026 could be the year of the foldable phone. Samsung and Google already have models on the market, and Apple is reportedly planning to drop its version in September. But are consumers willing to shell out $2,000 for a little extra screen? NBC News chief tech analyst Joanna Stern explains why the phones have appeal.

Rasuwagadhi Hydro provided Rs 500,000 per family to employees who went missing or died in the Bhotekoshi flood. The Nepali community in North Alabama donated $50,000 to the Prime Minister's Relief Fund for flood victims, while the New Zealand-Nepal Society contributed Rs 12.6 million for relief and rehabilitation. The government also declared flood-affected local levels in Gorkha, Baglung, and Dhading as disaster crisis areas.
New reports highlight the ongoing psychological and logistical recovery from the Bagmati floods. An article warns that graphic flood videos on social media are increasing mental stress among children, while UNICEF is working to meet the urgent needs of over 32,000 affected children. A feature story details the difficult resettlement prospects facing survivors like Chheku Lama, who lost his home in the disaster.

logs.summary: Severe monsoon rains and cyclones have caused widespread flooding across the Philippines, particularly in Luzon, with damage nearing P4 billion in Central Luzon and P2.68 billion in infrastructure damage in the Ilocos Region, affecting over four million people. At least two brothers drowned in a submerged bypass road in Pampanga, and a baby was dramatically rescued from flash floods in Manila. In response, lawmakers are pushing for flood control master plan reviews and Senate investigations into the government's disaster response.

news.headline: Storms cause 5 deaths in Mexico as flood risk eases in southwestern US

Authorities said Monday that five people have died in Mexico due to the hurricane and the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel. Rachel caused street flooding and other damage in Mexico’s Baja California state. Four people died after Rachel swept through over the weekend and at least six were missing. The storm's remnants also caused flooding in the southwestern U.S. The risk had mostly ended by Monday evening. Power was gradually being restored after Hurricane Isaias hit the U.S. Southeast.
